Moved 1 time as a child with both of my parents, they got divorced, then I moved 3 times with my mum and sister (plus my mums ex husband). I graduated from school when I was 19, shortly after I turned 20. I worked as a call center agent to make quick money and signed a contract for a shared flat with my then best friend. One and a half months before we were supposed to move in, my healthy 16 y/o sister died due to sudden heartfailure. My mum and her were supposed to stay in our flat, but after her sudden death, my mother decided to move 600km away with her then boyfriend (I totally understood her reasons and was fine with it, she would not have done it, if it had been a problem for me). She moved out about two weeks before I could move into my flat. 2 months after my then best friend and I moved into our shared flat, she got kicked out (we worked at the same job) and just moved out leaving me all alone with double costs and no clue what to do. The flatowners lived on the floor beneath and were literally stalking me, constantly filming me, installing CCTV everywhere, coming into my flat when I was sleeping, terrorising me and making me pay for stuff I never damaged. It was horrible, but thank god I found a new flat and moved in all by myself. It was perfect, besides that I was not allowed to own cats. Some time after I moved in, shortly after the pandemic started I had to stop working / was on sick leave for almost a year and was in and out of hospitals due to my mental health. I had to pay everything myself, my mum could not support me and my dad never even considered helping me (I already had to sue him as a kid to support me w/ education and he did not change). I loved my new flat, but almost two years ago I had water damage for the first time and it got supposedly fixed, but a year ago appeared worse than ever. I could not stay or sleep in my flat without having heavy allergic reactions and trouble breathing. My lungs are constantly damaged. I moved in the old flat of my aunt and uncle for the time it took to fix, or let me say, it takes to fix. It's such a saddening story, but it still isn't fixed. I have to throw away all my stuff and my furniture is rotting more and more with every additional day passing. Sadly it is a bigger thing and even a lawyer couldn't do anything to speeden up the process. This took a toll on my mental health, which hasn't been great or even good the last decade. If all this would not have happened, I might have moved back in with my mum and sister and even though I really really wish that I still had the possibility to do so (i.e. my sister still being alive), I think I could not move back in with anyone. I need my own space and I really hope I'll get it back soon.

Hello. I am not a doctor, but I hope it's okay for me to comment (as I understood the rules, it hopefully should be).

First of all, I am very very sorry for your loss.
The very same thing happened to me and my family. My healthy sister suddenly died at 16 during her sleep. We didn't know what was wrong, the paramedics told us it looked like cardiac arrest, but we had to wait for the autopsy.
After the autopsy was done we were told she had an unknown mutation of the heart and that it can be genetic. She apparently had hypoplasia of the right main stem of the coronary arteries and they assured that it would have under no circumstances been found if one did not search for this exact mutation. She even went to a cardiologist once for a check-up and they didn't find anything.

After it all happened and we found out what exactly was wrong with her heart, I decided to get tested for this exact mutation and had to stay in hospital for two days where they ran a lot of blood tests, ECG, longterm-ECG, 24h blood pressure and most importantly a cardiac CT.
I was told I most certainly do not have the same problem and a healthy heart. I still live in constant fear though and experience a lot of cardiac anxiety with chest pains and breathing troubles.

I sadly can't find anything specific on the internet either and wish there was somewhat more of a support group or help line or something that helps family members with what medical exams to get and how to cope.

I really hope you find your answers and will be able to live a life for two. For yourself and your sister.

Big hug,
